texts: A post-infarction ventricular septal defect with cardiogenic shock, two vasopressors, intubation and rising creatinine is best managed first with veno-arterial ECMO.
VA-ECMO restores flow to the organs at once and lets the infarcted septum firm up before the defect is repaired.
Repair in the first days of shock, through friable necrotic muscle, carries a very high mortality and a high rate of residual defects.
A left ventricular assist device alone does not support the failing right side and can draw blood across the defect from right to left.
Catheter closure of a 2.5 cm defect in fresh necrotic muscle often fails.
In the picture, Chopper's trolley of gills brings the lights back on, and a rope bridge leads to the hole, while the surgeon's toolbox stays locked.
Memory hook: gills first, the needle later.
